CodeEditor from ui-components is a text area shown as a code editor, CodeMirror, in the colors of the theme and the look of the page. Choose a language: Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, JSON and Markdown are built in, Markdown highlighting its fenced code blocks in their own languages, and the log is a grammar this page plugs in with a script of its own. Ctrl+F searches and replaces, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+S saves, Alt and the mouse select a rectangle, and the arrows in the gutter fold blocks. Tab indents: Escape, then Tab, leaves the editor.

The server keeps each sample in the session: its text, which it follows as you type, and the state of its editor, where the cursor is, what you selected, how far you scrolled and the size you gave it by the bar along its bottom. The sentence below the editor says what the server knows. Switch languages, or leave the page and come back, and each editor is where you left it. The check boxes and the drop-downs render the editor again via Ajax, and it goes on as it was.

Below the second pill, notes in Markdown show beside their preview, in a split panel: the preview follows the text as you type, with its tables, task lists and code blocks highlighted in their languages, and HTML in the text shows as text. Drag the divider to share the room, and the bar below to make both taller. The button hides the preview, giving the editor all the room, and shows it again. Tick Keep the preview in step, and the preview follows the place you are at in the editor: move the cursor, type or scroll, and the matching part of the preview comes into view. The session keeps it all.

Below the third pill the files of a project open in tabs, an editor in each. A file with changes not saved marks its tab, which the editor tells the tabs in the browser, and closing it asks first. Save it with Ctrl+S or the button. Switching tabs keeps where you were in each. Everything works under a strict Content Security Policy.
